Landing.badge: Group tours · Solo guides · Day planner
Landing.headline: Seoul, with someone who knows it.
Landing.subhead: Join a small group of travellers with a local guide, book a guide just for you, or let us order your day so you spend it exploring instead of backtracking.
Landing.firstTimeSubtitle: The six things worth sorting out before you land.

tmoney.title: Get a T-money card
tmoney.body: One tap card for subway, buses and even taxis. Buy it at any convenience store.

keta.title: Check K-ETA / visa
keta.body: Many visitors need a K-ETA before flying. Check your passport's rules early.

money.title: Cards work almost everywhere
money.body: Carry some cash for street food and markets; ATMs marked "Global" take foreign cards.

sim.title: eSIM or pocket Wi-Fi
sim.body: Maps and translation need data. Airport counters and eSIMs are quick to set up.

apps.title: Use Naver Map or KakaoMap
apps.body: Google Maps can't give walking directions in Korea. Papago translates menus from a photo.

help.title: Call 1330 for help
help.body: The free tourist helpline answers in English, Japanese, Chinese and more, 24/7.

faq.a1: A guide publishes a tour with a date, meeting point, stops and a price per person. You book seats, pay, and appear in the member list so everyone knows who's coming.
faq.a2: Not in this demo. Payments run in Stripe test mode, so use the test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 with any future date and CVC.
faq.q3: What's the difference between a group tour and a solo guide?
faq.a3: A group tour is shared with other travellers and priced per person. A solo guide is just you (and your party) on a date you choose, at the guide's own price.
faq.a4: Unpaid bookings can be cancelled any time. Paid group bookings can be cancelled for a refund up to 24 hours before the tour starts.
faq.q5: Do I need a guide to use the planner?
faq.a5: No. The day planner is free, needs no account, and works for any places on the map. Log in only if you want to save it.

Transport.title: Getting around Seoul
Transport.subtitle: Seoul's transit is cheap, clean and fast. Here's how to use it like a local.
Transport.tip1: Tap your T-money card when you get off the bus too; it's how transfers become free.
Transport.tip2: Subway trains stop around midnight. Night buses (N-numbered) run after that.
Transport.tip3: Use Naver Map or KakaoMap for walking and transit directions.
